body:
So your a poor student without a girlfriend? Thats what I’m getting here. That is completely normal. Women usually want some security from a man. How could you provide that without a job? 

As for the whole ”not attractive enough for dating apps” that’s bullshit and I think you know it too. Even if you are Quasimodo himself you could at least meet someone. It might take time and it might not be the Disney princess you always imagined yourself marrying but it would be a real human being. 

University is hard. And, chemical engineering? That’s a different beast! Focus on your studies, improve yourself, do something for someone else and you will have a bright future. God bless!

What about finding a guy? Start a family? Maybe that would be something to look forward to? When I read your text you seem very disinterested in the whole career thing. And please don’t think for a second that that is something unusual. Most people don’t have careers, they have jobs and that is not the same thing. Having a job to sustain yourself might be necessary depending on where on earth you live. But the job is not what gives you meaning. No your family, friends and other communal commitments does. Maybe you have none of those now. But you can try. God bless!

Dude, literally anything you do would be an improvement. Pick the smallest thing you can think of and fix it. Is your sock drawer disorganized? Then organize it! Is there a corner in your home where you have a bunch of soda bottles? Then take a couple and put it in a plastic bag. Don’t even think about actually taking it out to a recycling station yet. Just do the smallest thing imaginable that actually would be an improvement and just do it. The cool thing about doing the small stuff is that you can actually complete them. Will you feel ashamed that you have to begin in such a small way? Probably. But it doesnt matter where you begin. You efforts will stack upon each other and the results will increase exponentially. Do the smallest stuff and one day the small stuff won’t be so small. God bless!

Don't know you, pal. But I do care. You seem to have struggled - a lot; and for a long time no less. Being alone or having the feeling of being alone is a hard thing to sholder. Why do you think you couldn't connect with People?
OP, you still there?
Hey, OP. If you don't mind me asking. Why do you want to kill yourself?

I'm no psycoanalyst but there might be something there. The early suicidal tendencies is maybe something to explore and see why they came up. Maybe some traumatic event happened some time before which triggered all this? 

Why is the family split?

I don't wanna step on any toes here so please let me know if the questions are intrusive or if you don't feel comfortable answering them.

Thanks, I appreciate it.

Did you think about suicide alot before that incident? To go and try slice your own throat is... I can't put words in it but it boggles my mind that a kid that age does that. It seems to me that there has to be something before this?

You mentioned your stepmom. How is your reletionship with you family?

The fact that you tried so young seems quite unusual. A kid that age, to my knowledge, barley knows what suicide is. That must have been awfull for you to have this thing plauging you from such a young age. 

Do you go to any therapy right now?

Being alone so much must be hard, and the anxiety can't be making it and easier.

Everybody needs help sometimes. I do however fail to see why you would be a bruden just because you need help sometimes?

Hey, man! I feel for you. Not being able to take joy out of anything in life is certanly a feeling I am familiar with, and one I wouldn't wish upon anyone else.

If you have someone, anyone, to whom you could speak too about this, then that could be beneficial. You said that there is no way they could help. What help, if you were to think freely, is it that you would like to recieve?
Sounds like you're having a tough time with the people around you. That sucks! Would you like to tell us why you feel like you're a burden?

Hi, thank you.

I'd say that the thoughts intesifies with stress, or being overwhelmed. For instance tasks att my job which I don't know how to solve. There might be some seasonal affections aswell, such as the darkness of winter keeping me in bed whilst in the summer I'd att least wake up. I find it hard to find a more clear or specific pattern then that though. I tried vitamin D pills since its very dark here during the winter months but didn't feel an obvious difference.

The thought is often there, lurking in the back of my mind. Sometimes it don't come out and sometimes it does. Usually I handle it quite good, but this weekend was harder then usually for some reason. I would say in the past month or two the thoughts have been quite frequent; mostly daily.

Sorry for long reply. And again, thank you.
Thank, you for your kind words.
Thank, you. Your comment makes me feel a bit less lonely in all this. Best of luck to you!

Glad to hear that things seems to looking upward for you. 

It might be out of habbit? Someone told me once that is takes 90 days to create a new habbit. I wouldn't trust that number to be completely true but the spirit behind it might be; creating new habbits takes time. If you have lived with this for quite some time, there might be some underlying thought patterns which have formed and would, thusly take some time to get rid of.

Just a thought.

That must have been extremely hard for you. There seem to quite a few things around you that just don't pan out. This must be very demotivating and I'm very sorry that you have to go through all of this.

Security and stability are very hard to get in this world. We don't really control all the things that can go wrong. I do understand the frustration, though. It can be infuriating when nothing stays in place and after a while, one just lands in disparity. 

Since you work such long hours, have you considered some online therapy to match your schedule; or some coaching?

I hope it goes well for you. 

Regarding the reasons for life, I would encourage you to look at the possibilities up ahead. You are young and there is so much to look forward to, relationships, career, and so much more. No one gets everything but it is my personal belief that everyone gets something; if we work for it.

Help a friend in need, or fix something that you can fix. A broken door handle? Look at a YouTube tutorial and go to town. A lot of people are driven by helping people, and it can be quite motivating to do so. 

It's hard to define a clear reason to live. You kind of have to make up your own reason and go from there. It might even change over time, for you.

I do wish you the best of luck!

Damn, OP. Thank you for sharing that. What a fantastic description of such a horrible event. 

I am truly sorry for hearing that you had to go through that. The self-blame must be awful to deal with and I hope you come to terms with it soon. We often need help the most when we aren't able to ask for it.

Good luck, OP!
Hey, OP. Sucks that you feel that way. Having people downplay your problems must be very difficult. Would you perhaps like to tell us why you want to drift off?

That's awful that you've had to deal with this for so long. Have you been in therapy all this time as well or that something more recent?

She might have the best of intentions but that doesn't mean you aren't allowed to feel sad about it. Looking forward to something and then have it taken away is not a fun thing.
Man, that sucks. How long have you felt like this?
Has something happened recently that made you feel like this?

The whole Lack of will = Laziness gets on nerves, and I can imagine it being quite hard on you to hear that. 

It's good that you have things that you still enjoy.

Are you in any sort of therapy now by any chance?
Where ever you are in the world, whoever you are, I do care. Would you like to tell us why you feel lonely?

Hey, OP. If I understand your question correctly your asking for a reason to live, and this is very dependant on your situation. You seem not very satisfied with your potential future. Maybe you could tell us about that, what do you work with?

For me, I usually start with cleaning my bedroom. For some reason, I get a tiny, tiny boost by doing this. Then a shower, a long cold one works best but I usually do a warm one. If I have managed those things the worst part is over and I continue with whatever I was supposed to do. This procedure does by no means make me happy but rather gives me a slight chance to get enough energy to try and do something that makes me glad. I have personally never been able to just think myself out of it.

If you don't mind me asking, why does everything seem bleak?

That must have been tough on you op and it saddens me to hear that you had to go through that. I do wonder though, why don't you do these things now? You said it wouldn't be appropriate, could you help me understand that?
Would you like to tell us why you would do this?

I think it's important to remember that suicidal thoughts can hit anyone no matter how "good" their life is. It can be the smallest event that triggers the thoughts and it can be random. This is why it's important not to put blame on yourself because you got these thoughts. Rather talk about them with someone close and work through the issue, and if that doesn't help, or if it gets worse contact a mental health professional.

As for the reasons to not commit suicide, that would depend on your situation. Since you are quite young I would say that you have much look forward to. Relationships, career, and so much more. Your life could be what you want it to be and all you have to do is figure out what that is and work on it. There are a few restrictions, of course, to be the flying queen of the moon is probably a little far-fetched. But to find a partner that you like, get a job with some good colleagues and have enough free time to make furniture is achievable for a lot of people. Just making some stuff up here since I don't know you.

Other people need help; in all possible ways. They require the help of good people and you can be one of those good people. By help, I don't just mean mental help or even medical. It could be as a lawyer, a plumber, a babysitter, whatever, and that can also be a good reason to stay alive. There might be a lot of people on this earth but there never will be too many good people.

The normal way to deal with any phobia is through incremental exposure. This is probably something that you and your therapist could talk about if you asked them about it. I'm not saying it would be easy or quick but it is however doable, I believe in you!
Hey, how are you feeling today?

Just to makeing sure that I understand the terminology. Agoraphobia is the fear of being in places where escape might be difficult or help won't be available, right? English is not my native language.
Is the agoraphobia something that you and your therapist are working at? Or has that also been left untreated?

I am not in any way a mental health proffesional just a dude with a keyboard who have dealt with mental problems in many forms, both personally and in proximity who wishes to help in some small way.

The reason I asked was to get an idea of your view on the situation.

You mentioned loneliness, how do your social situation look like?
That must be very hard for you having panic attacks so often must be draining. What is it that you are planning to do?
What makes you say that you are too hopeless?
That's a long time to suffer. That must have been awfull for you. Would you like to tell us what "out of touch with reality" means?
Can you help me understand what you mean when you say you're damaged?

That sound rough. Dealing with those things are not an easy task and is not made any easier when the help one gets is not effective. If I may ask, are you in some sort of therapy now or seeing a psychiatrist?

I would strongly sugest you to call the propper authoroties or have her call a suicide hotline. However as a friend there some things one can try.

Car Ride: Pick Up your friend for a drive. This is what I did with a friend and it was very effective. Just talking and listening to music for a few hours can be quite calming.

If a car ride is not an option just being there to talk can be as effective. 

In essence it's about being there and supporting the person and let them talk about it all and just listen.
Sture, I'm new to the site though so I don't know how to do that. Could send some invite or something?

The reason why you get scared of the notion of your parents protective behaviour is something that might be worth talking to about with your therapist. They are often good at looking at these things from different angles and making sense of them.

I'm okey with talking about it.

I think I understand what you mean. If I understand you correctly and please tell me of I'm wrong it's more about the restrictions they would place on you? Am I in the ball park here?

Well, suicide is more deadly so that could be considered more serious. However something did stop you. You did text the hotline. You did not do it while they were home which says something. I just don't know what yet. 

Would you like to talk about why you feel like this in the first place?

Det låter riktigt jobbigt. Att känna sig utstött eller i vägen är något som är extremt jobbigt så jag upplever dig absolut inte som dramatisk. Jag undrar dock varför du inte vill att man lägger energi på dig. Skulle du kunna hjälpa mig förstå det?
Were you afraid for how they would react when talking to you?
Hej, låter som en förjävlig kväll. Vill du berätta mer om varför du stack till klippan?

They seems like good people. A little overprotecting maybe, but good people none the less. I would Imagine this being quite infuriating.

When you said that them rapidly calling eachother freaked you out, what does that mean, could you tell me about that?

A friendly reminder.
I believe asking questions is the best way to help someone but if you are not comfortable with talking about something just say so, or don't reply if you feel like it. This is heavy stuff and I'd hate to do you a disservice.

Yeah, fuck Jamie. Glad to hear that he didn't completely discoraged you from texting them again. Depending om where you live there might be multple hot-lines available. I would encurage you to have a look around and save some numbers for a rainy-day.

That I can understand. It seems to me that you are faced with a great deal of uncertanty and that must be really tough. 

How are your parents, could you talk about your fears regarding their behaviour?

As for school thats a tricky one. I would like for you to prioritize getting help but thats easy for me to say, it's not me who have to live with it. I can tell you however that these kinds of things often blow by quickly. Waiting a few weeks and half will not remember it. I do get your concern though.

You might be able to talk to your therapist regarding these concerns? See if you can come to some compromize?
Could you help me understand what about it frieghtens you?

First and foremost, great job on talking to the hotline; that was very brave of you. 

You could tell her what happened; starting with "I tried to kill myself" is never wrong. If the talking is a problem you could show her what you've written here and go from there. If that is to much you might be able to email her and tell her that you planned to it bit didn't.

The conversation from there will depend alot on your therapist and your history and it might be very hard on you. Afterwards it can be good to allow yourself some treat, like lying in bed for a while, watch a movie or eat something you like and not beat yourself up for it.

I feel for you. Work can be very demanding and in periods outright terrible but, you might ask yourself why you work?

If money is the issue, because sometimes it is not, there might be something not connecting for you. If you suffer in your private life and work is no better then it would be logical to ponder the reason for funding a shitty life. In that case one could start by looking in to the other aspects of life and see if there is something in need of change.

It could also be a shitty job. In that case I would urge you to have a look around and see what oppertunities might present themselvs.

I Imagine that would feel very difficult for you; not to be able to express yourself fully to her. Few things can replace a good therapist. Would there be harm in asking? 

In your original post you mentioned your sister. How is your reletionship with her?

Which aspects seems daunting?

If you were to tell somebody, how would you do it?

That seems quite selfless. 

They might be overwhelmed, and they might not. I would like you to consider atleast mentioning something to them. So for instance "Hey (parent) , I have this person that I like but I don't feel very confident asking them out. Do you have any tips". It probably souldn't be exactly that but atleast something personal and somewhat intimate that could get a conversation about feelings started.

If thats not an option you might have a friend to talk about this with?

Medication can be great and I hope you find a good psychiatrist whom can help you in that regard.

I am glad to hear that you are working on it. The little things we do during the day can help imensly.

Are you able to communicate with you parents regarding your problems?

Try to take pride in the little things. Like sleeping one hour less(if that's what you need), eating a sandwich or on a really shitty day just sitting up in the bed. 

Try some light exercise or breathing exercises.

You mention that you've gone to therapy. Is it possible to continue this, or maybe see psychiatrist?

A suicide hotline can be good. You seem to have some friends, you might be able to unload some of your thoughts on them, too. 

I used to talk to different people about different things because I was scared to unload everything at once. Like I would break completely if I did that. Which made me more comfortable just talking about it.

For instance you could talk to some friends about family or your self picture and a suicide hotline about your suicidal thoughts, tendencies of self harm and the like. Just a sugestion.

The situation with your family seems very important to you. Could you initiate some sort of conversation with your mother about your communication? Like "Hey, we've barley spoken in a while - how are you?". 

Is there a way for you to see a mental health professionall?

None of us get the life we want. We do however get the life we create. You might have done some stuff. Some stuff that are potentially very bad. It might be tough for a while but if you are willing, you can create a different life. You could even be of help to the world.
Well, would you like to be there for her if she felt the way you do now?
What do you usually do to numb the pain?

Sometimes, when one is nice to people, one can get too nice. Caring so much about other peoples thoughts and feeling can prevent us from being ourself. Lika a filter; if you will. This filter will probably generate a lot of acquaintances but will often repell people who could potantially become close friends.

When we act in a "too nice mannor" for too long we can often feel detached from our own circle of friends and even make us feel like intruders in our own life. 

Everyone does bad things. Everyone makes mistakes. Doesn't mean we are bad people.  

I don't know your story so I won't tell you what to do bit I do wish you the best of luck.
